claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children. Let me start with the first one:

**How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm enquiring about my child Alex. Just the one.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're enquiring about one child, Alex.

To help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather a bit more information about your circumstances.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex was born in 2005, so he's 19 now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So Alex is 19 years old, born in 2005.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about Alex's current situation.

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education. He's doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Thank you for clarifying that Alex is in full-time education doing A-levels.

I need to ask one more question to complete my assessment:

**Are you the person with responsibility for Alex (such as a parent or guardian), and do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and Alex lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me explain the outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: Alex is 19 years old and in full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college). Child Benefit can be paid for young people over 16 who are in approved full-time education or training. Since Alex meets this requirement and lives with you in the UK, you qualify to receive Child Benefit for them.

If you'd like to proceed with a claim, you can apply through the UK government's Child Benefit application process.

reasonings: Alex is 19 years old and in full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college). Under Child Benefit rules, a young person can continue to receive Child Benefit beyond age 16 if they are in approved full-time education or training. Since Alex is in full-time education and living with their parent in the UK, they meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. As Alex's parent, you have responsibility for a child who is in full-time education in the UK, which qualifies them for Child Benefit entitlement."]
